target_body: Promo pricing: new accts +31%, booked rev +18%, price-sensitive buyers, first-term renewals -12pp; billing mix constant.
system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Promo pricing: new accts +31%, booked rev +18%, price-sensitive buyers, first-term renewals -12pp; billing mix constant.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Promo pricing: new accts +31%, booked rev +18%, price-sensitive buyers, first-term renewals -12pp; billing mix constant.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure to match with promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is the one inherited record that actually traces a growth tactic through to downstream value, and it is unfavorable: +31% new accounts and +18% booked revenue bought at the cost of -12pp first-term renewals among price-sensitive buyers. That is precisely the buyer segment the competitor is taking, so a promo would concentrate acquisition in the cohort with the worst demonstrated retention — booked revenue up, sustainable qualified revenue likely down. I am declining that direction rather than spending verification on it.

The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at memory_86/memory_31 (onboarding and signup simplification) and memory_91 (in-product activation messaging). I am spending both verification pulls there because those are the memories I intend to act on, and because their summaries share a specific weakness: every reported outcome is a proxy — completion rate, time-to-value, week-one engagement, 'first meaningful action.' None is stated in terms of retained or qualified revenue. memory_57 by contrast explicitly checked retention and found no harm, which shows the archive is capable of recording that check; its absence in 86/91 is informative. So I want the source records for memory_86 and memory_91 to see (a) whether the lifts were ever followed through to revenue or renewal, (b) the baseline cohort and whether it resembles today's mix, and (c) whether the onboarding shortening removed steps that were doing qualifying work — a shorter funnel can raise completion while lowering the quality of who completes, which would show up later as exactly the activation decline we are now seeing. It is worth holding open that the current 4-6% declines may be partly a downstream consequence of prior simplification wins rather than an independent problem for more simplification to solve.

I intend simplify_onboarding at standard experiment scale: it is supported by two independent inherited records (memory_31, memory_86), it plausibly addresses both declining metrics since onboarding feeds activation, and it does not buy volume by degrading cohort quality the way a promo would. I am not going broad — the supporting evidence is proxy-only and possibly stale at day 12/52. Instrumentation must carry revenue-linked and renewal-linked endpoints, not completion rate alone, so this run repairs the measurement gap in the memories it relies on. If verification shows memory_86's lift never touched revenue or came from a materially different cohort, I would drop to a small guarded test or switch to activation_messaging as the more direct fit to the larger (-6%) decline. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is real but aimed at a segment that is not the one under attack, and it does not address either declining metric this week.
